levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The conclusion is stated as certain when the scenario does not support that.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Uncertainty is mentioned in general terms only.

judgment.prompt: The headline is literally true and still misleads. Explain how, then rewrite it as a claim a shopper could verify before entering the store.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Explains that "up to" describes the maximum across the sale, not the typical discount, and that 11 of the 12 items are at 10%.
Uses the 14.2% average, or the 1-in-12 count, to show how unrepresentative the 60% figure is.
Rewrites the claim in checkable terms — naming the typical discount, the number of items at each level, or which items are deeply discounted.
evidenceRequirements: Cites the item counts (1 at 60%, 11 at 10%) and at least one computed figure from this lesson.
lookFors: The rewritten claim is verifiable before purchase, not merely more modest in tone.
The response separates literal truth from the impression the claim creates.
judgment.commonMisconception: Judging an advertising claim only by whether it is technically false.

nonDiagnosticGuard: Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

oracle.method: every fixed answer above was recomputed from the item's own stated scenario parameters, not transcribed
oracle.arithmetic: exact rational arithmetic over BigInt; no binary floating point
oracle.limits: Recomputation establishes that the key follows from the stated figures. It does not by itself establish that the model chosen is the right model for the scenario; that is carried by the per-item reasoning, the parameter-visibility check, and human review.
